Photon-Counting CT Virtual Monoenergetic Imaging

A Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha scan of the Gammex 472, its four CdTe energy bins decomposed together, becomes virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) at 40, 70, 100 and 140 keV, checked rod by rod against theory.

The scanner is the Alpha model of the basis-spectral-denoising study: a CdTe detector that sorts every photon into four energy windows (thresholds 20 / 35 / 55 / 70 keV), a 140 kVp, 0.5 s axial acquisition at the dose of the physical Gammex scan, every view integrated over the arc the gantry turns while it is read, and that study's denoiser, reconstruction windows and spectral pair.

The Chain at a Glance

The phantom is projected once; the noise-free reference, a calibration draw and the measured draw all reuse that projection. Each simulate! returns the four corrected energy-bin sinograms and the air count of every ray in every bin, I0[col, row, bin], from which spectral_basis(ws; I0) builds the model the simulation applied. All four bins then enter one decomposition as separate measurements; nothing is merged into "low" and "high".

Figure Style

The colours, the theme and the drawing helpers every BasisSimulator notebook shares, then this notebook's own drawings: the Gammex 472, drawn from its label mask, a photon-counting dexel and the bowtie's fan.

# BasisSimulator's colours: the docs site's warm paper and ink, its violet and cyan accents
COLORS = (
    paper = Mke.RGBf(0.973, 0.969, 0.957), # #f8f7f4, every figure's background
    card = Mke.RGBf(0.941, 0.925, 0.894),  # #f0ece4, boxes in diagrams
    rule = Mke.RGBf(0.831, 0.816, 0.784),  # #d4d0c8, outlines and grid
    ink = Mke.RGBf(0.165, 0.145, 0.125),   # #2a2520, text
    muted = Mke.RGBf(0.42, 0.396, 0.376),  # #6b6560, secondary text
    night = Mke.RGBf(0.067, 0.067, 0.063), # #111110, the locator band
    night_card = Mke.RGBf(0.137, 0.129, 0.122),
    night_ink = Mke.RGBf(0.94, 0.925, 0.894),
    night_muted = Mke.RGBf(0.62, 0.6, 0.57),
    violet = Mke.RGBf(0.486, 0.227, 0.929),      # #7c3aed, BasisSimulator itself
    violet_soft = Mke.RGBf(0.867, 0.839, 0.996), # #ddd6fe
    cyan = Mke.RGBf(0.031, 0.569, 0.698),        # #0891b2, measurements and data
    cyan_soft = Mke.RGBf(0.647, 0.953, 0.988),   # #a5f3fc
    beam = Mke.RGBf(0.96, 0.62, 0.14),           # x rays
    red = Mke.RGBf(0.796, 0.235, 0.2),           # Julia red: calcium, failures
    green = Mke.RGBf(0.22, 0.596, 0.149),        # Julia green: iodine, passes
    blue = Mke.RGBf(0.251, 0.388, 0.847),        # Julia blue: water, references
    purple = Mke.RGBf(0.584, 0.345, 0.698),      # Julia purple
);
# Large, uncluttered type on warm paper for every figure
THEME = Mke.Theme(
    fontsize = 18,
    backgroundcolor = COLORS.paper,
    textcolor = COLORS.ink,
    figure_padding = (12, 24, 12, 12),
    palette = (color = [
        COLORS.violet,
        COLORS.cyan,
        COLORS.beam,
        COLORS.red,
        COLORS.green,
        COLORS.blue,
        COLORS.purple,
    ],),
    Axis = (
        backgroundcolor = COLORS.paper,
        titlesize = 22,
        titlealign = :left,
        titlegap = 12,
        subtitlesize = 17,
        subtitlecolor = COLORS.muted,
        xlabelsize = 19,
        ylabelsize = 19,
        xticklabelsize = 16,
        yticklabelsize = 16,
        xgridcolor = (COLORS.ink, 0.07),
        ygridcolor = (COLORS.ink, 0.07),
        leftspinecolor = COLORS.rule,
        bottomspinecolor = COLORS.rule,
        xtickcolor = COLORS.rule,
        ytickcolor = COLORS.rule,
        topspinevisible = false,
        rightspinevisible = false,
        xlabelpadding = 8,
        ylabelpadding = 12,
    ),
    Legend = (
        labelsize = 17,
        framevisible = false,
        backgroundcolor = COLORS.paper,
        patchsize = (30, 14),
        rowgap = 8,
    ),
    Colorbar = (labelsize = 18, ticklabelsize = 15),
    Lines = (linewidth = 2.5,),
);
begin
    """A blank drawing area at `position`: equal scales, no axes, limits `(x0, x1, y0, y1)`."""
    function canvas(position, limits; background = COLORS.paper)
        ax = Mke.Axis(position; aspect = Mke.DataAspect(), backgroundcolor = background)
        Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
        Mke.hidespines!(ax)
        Mke.limits!(ax, limits...)
        return ax
    end

    """The corners of a rectangle centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, its corners rounded by `r`."""
    function rounded_rect(c, w, h, r)
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = c[1] - w / 2, c[2] - h / 2, c[1] + w / 2, c[2] + h / 2
        r = min(r, w / 2, h / 2)
        arc(cx, cy, θ0) = [
            Mke.Point2f(cx + r * cos(θ), cy + r * sin(θ))
            for θ in range(θ0, θ0 + π / 2; length = 8)
        ]
        return vcat(
            arc(x1 - r, y0 + r, -π / 2),
            arc(x1 - r, y1 - r, 0.0),
            arc(x0 + r, y1 - r, π / 2),
            arc(x0 + r, y0 + r, π),
        )
    end

    """A straight arrow from `a` to `b`; `head` is the arrowhead's size in pixels."""
    function arrow!(
        ax,
        a,
        b;
        color = COLORS.muted,
        linewidth = 2.5,
        head = 15,
        linestyle = :solid,
    )
        a, b = Mke.Point2f(a), Mke.Point2f(b)
        Mke.lines!(ax, [a, b]; color, linewidth, linestyle)
        t = b - a
        Mke.scatter!(
            ax,
            [b];
            marker = :utriangle,
            markersize = head,
            rotation = atan(t[2], t[1]) - π / 2,
            color,
            markerspace = :pixel,
        )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A box in a flow chart: centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, a bold `title` and an optional smaller
    `subtitle`. `accent` colours its outline (and a strip down its left edge).
    """
    function node!(
        ax,
        c,
        title;
        subtitle = "",
        w = 3.0,
        h = 1.0,
        accent = COLORS.violet,
        fill = COLORS.card,
        textcolor = COLORS.ink,
        subcolor = COLORS.muted,
        titlesize = 19,
        subtitlesize = 15,
        code = false,
    )
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            rounded_rect(c, w, h, 0.14);
            color = fill,
            strokecolor = accent,
            strokewidth = 2,
        )
        strip = rounded_rect((c[1] - w / 2 + 0.06, c[2]), 0.12, h - 0.1, 0.05)
        Mke.poly!(ax, strip; color = accent)
        font = code ? "DejaVu Sans Mono Bold" : :bold
        dy = isempty(subtitle) ? 0.0 : 0.17 * h
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            c[1] + 0.05,
            c[2] + dy;
            text = title,
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = titlesize,
            font,
            color = textcolor,
        )
        isempty(subtitle) ||
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                c[1] + 0.05,
                c[2] - 0.22 * h;
                text = subtitle,
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = subtitlesize,
                color = subcolor,
            )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A flow chart: `nodes` maps a key to `(x, y, title, subtitle, accent)` (subtitle and accent
    optional), `edges` lists `from => to` pairs, drawn as arrows between the boxes' edges, and
    `labels` (optional) puts a note on an edge. Returns the canvas.
    """
    function flow_chart!(position, nodes, edges; limits, w = 3.0, h = 1.0, labels = Dict())
        ax = canvas(position, limits)
        box(key) = nodes[key]
        function port(from, to)
            a, b = box(from), box(to)
            if abs(b[2] - a[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # side by side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            elseif abs(b[1] - a[1]) < 1.0e-6
                # one above the other
                s = sign(b[2] - a[2])
                return (a[1], a[2] + s * h / 2), (b[1], b[2] - s * h / 2)
            else
                # leave sideways, arrive on the facing side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            end
        end
        for (from, to) in edges
            p, q = port(from, to)
            if abs(p[1] - q[1]) < 1.0e-6 || abs(p[2] - q[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # straight across or straight down
                arrow!(ax, p, q)
            else
                # a right-angled connector: across to the gap's middle, along it, then in
                mx = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
                Mke.lines!(
                    ax,
                    Mke.Point2f[p, (mx, p[2]), (mx, q[2])];
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                    linewidth = 2.5,
                )
                arrow!(ax, (mx, q[2]), q)
            end
            haskey(labels, from => to) &&
                Mke.text!(
                    ax,
                    (p[1] + q[1]) / 2,
                    q[2] + 0.12;
                    text = labels[from => to],
                    align = (:center, :bottom),
                    fontsize = 15,
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                )
        end
        for (_, n) in nodes
            node!(
                ax,
                (n[1], n[2]),
                n[3];
                subtitle = length(n) >= 4 ? n[4] : "",
                accent = length(n) >= 5 ? n[5] : COLORS.violet,
                w,
                h,
            )
        end
        return ax
    end

    """
    A CT gantry seen along z, centred at the origin: the source(s) at radius `sid` (one per entry
    of `angles`, degrees), the fan, the detector arc at `sdd` from each source, and a round object
    of radius `r_object`. Draws on `ax` in the colours of `dark` (the locator band) or paper.
    """
    function gantry!(
        ax;
        sid = 5.4,
        sdd = 9.5,
        angles = (90.0,),
        fan_deg = 50.0,
        r_object = 2.0,
        detector_colors = (COLORS.cyan,),
        labels = ("Tube",),
        dark = true,
        object = true,
    )
        ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
        ring = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
        Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid + 0.9); color = ring)
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid - 1.6);
            color = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper,
        )
        for (k, θ) in enumerate(angles)
            θ = deg2rad(θ)
            s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
            half = deg2rad(fan_deg / 2)
            # the fan, from the focal spot to the detector arc (a circle about the source)
            edge = Mke.Point2f[
                s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
                for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
            ]
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Point2f.(vcat([s], edge));
                color = (COLORS.beam, 0.22),
                strokewidth = 0,
            )
            Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = detector_colors[mod1(k, end)], linewidth = 9)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                s * 1.18;
                text = labels[mod1(k, end)],
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = 17,
                font = :bold,
                color = ink,
            )
        end
        object &&
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), r_object);
                color = (COLORS.blue, 0.55),
                strokecolor = ink,
                strokewidth = 1.5,
            )
        return ax
    end

    """
    The dark locator band that opens a notebook: `n` panels side by side, each a canvas with
    `limits`, its `titles[i]` and `subtitles[i]` underneath. Returns the figure and the canvases;
    draw into them, then show the figure.
    """
    function locator_band(titles, subtitles; limits, size = (1500, 560))
        fig = Mke.Figure(;
            size,
            backgroundcolor = COLORS.night,
            figure_padding = (10, 10, 18, 10),
        )
        axes = [
            canvas(fig[1, i], limits[i]; background = COLORS.night)
            for i in eachindex(titles)
        ]
        for i in eachindex(titles)
            Mke.Label(
                fig[2, i],
                titles[i];
                fontsize = 25,
                font = :bold,
                color = COLORS.night_ink,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
            Mke.Label(
                fig[3, i],
                subtitles[i];
                fontsize = 17,
                color = COLORS.night_muted,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
        end
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 1, 8)
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 2, 2)
        return fig, axes
    end
end;
# the four energy bins' colours, from the lowest bin to the highest
BIN_COLORS = [COLORS.violet, COLORS.blue, COLORS.cyan, COLORS.green];
gammex_layout

The Gammex 472 as the drawings show it: its body radius and every rod's centre and radius (cm, about the centre of the image), measured from the phantom's own label mask.

"""
The Gammex 472 as the drawings show it: its body radius and every rod's centre and radius
(cm, about the centre of the image), measured from the phantom's own label mask.
"""
function gammex_layout(phantom)
    mask = phantom.mask[:, :, (size(phantom.mask, 3) + 1) ÷ 2]
    voxel = phantom.voxel_size[1]
    centre = (size(mask, 1) + 1) / 2
    function rod(label)
        pixels = findall(==(UInt8(label)), mask)
        return (
            x = (mean(p -> p[1], pixels) - centre) * voxel,
            y = (mean(p -> p[2], pixels) - centre) * voxel,
            r = sqrt(length(pixels) / π) * voxel,
        )
    end
    return (
        body = sqrt(count(!=(0x00), mask) / π) * voxel,
        voxel = voxel,
        Ca = [rod(label) for label in 10:16],
        I = [rod(label) for label in 20:26],
        Ca_names = ["50", "100", "200", "300", "400", "500", "600"],
        I_names = ["2", "2.5", "5", "7.5", "10", "15", "20"],
    )
end
gammex!

Draws the Gammex 472 of layout on ax: the solid-water body, calcium rods in red and iodine rods in green. show picks what stands out: :all, :water (with region, a mask on the phantom's image grid, drawn in cyan), :Ca or :I (those rods, named by concentration, each with its ROI of radius roi cm); the rest is faded.

"""
Draws the Gammex 472 of `layout` on `ax`: the solid-water body, calcium rods in red and iodine
rods in green. `show` picks what stands out: `:all`, `:water` (with `region`, a mask on the
phantom's image grid, drawn in cyan), `:Ca` or `:I` (those rods, named by concentration, each with
its ROI of radius `roi` cm); the rest is faded.
"""
function gammex!(ax, layout; show = :all, region = nothing, roi = 0.55, dark = false)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    faded(group) = show in (:all, group) ? 1.0 : 0.25
    disk(x, y, r) = Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(x, y), r)
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        disk(0, 0, layout.body);
        color = (COLORS.blue, show == :water ? 0.25 : 0.55),
        strokecolor = ink,
        strokewidth = 1.5,
    )
    if show == :water && region !== nothing
        xs = ((1:size(region, 1)) .- (size(region, 1) + 1) / 2) .* layout.voxel
        ys = ((1:size(region, 2)) .- (size(region, 2) + 1) / 2) .* layout.voxel
        Mke.heatmap!(
            ax,
            xs,
            ys,
            [inside ? 1.0f0 : NaN32 for inside in region];
            colormap = [COLORS.cyan, COLORS.cyan],
            colorrange = (0, 1),
            nan_color = :transparent,
        )
    end
    for (group, color) in ((:Ca, COLORS.red), (:I, COLORS.green))
        rods = getfield(layout, group)
        names = getfield(layout, Symbol(group, :_names))
        offset = group == :Ca ? 2.3 : 2.6
        for (rod, name) in zip(rods, names)
            Mke.poly!(ax, disk(rod.x, rod.y, rod.r); color = (color, faded(group)))
            show == group || continue
            Mke.lines!(
                ax,
                disk(rod.x, rod.y, roi);
                color = COLORS.paper,
                linewidth = 2,
                linestyle = :dash,
            )
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                rod.x * (1 + offset / hypot(rod.x, rod.y)),
                rod.y * (1 + offset / hypot(rod.x, rod.y));
                text = name,
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = 15,
                font = :bold,
                color = ink,
            )
        end
    end
    return ax
end
counting_dexel!

A photon-counting dexel at work, on ax (a canvas about (-0.5, 25, -1.6, 10.4)): a photon of energy keV stops in the CdTe, its charge drifts to the dexel's anode, and the pulse it makes is compared with every threshold of thresholds (keV): the highest it crosses decides the bin whose counter goes up by one.

"""
A photon-counting dexel at work, on `ax` (a canvas about `(-0.5, 25, -1.6, 10.4)`): a photon of
`energy` keV stops in the CdTe, its charge drifts to the dexel's anode, and the pulse it makes is
compared with every threshold of `thresholds` (keV): the highest it crosses decides the bin
whose counter goes up by one.
"""
function counting_dexel!(
    ax;
    energy = 62.0,
    thresholds = (20, 35, 55, 70),
    pulse = true,
    dark = false,
)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    muted = dark ? COLORS.night_muted : COLORS.muted
    card = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
    label(
        x,
        y,
        text;
        align = (:center, :center),
        size = 16,
        bold = false,
        color = ink,
    ) = Mke.text!(
        ax,
        x,
        y;
        text,
        align,
        fontsize = size,
        font = bold ? :bold : :regular,
        color,
    )

    # the dexel: CdTe between the cathode and its pixel anode
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        Mke.Rect2f(0.4, 1.8, 4.2, 5.4);
        color = (COLORS.violet_soft, dark ? 0.35 : 1.0),
    )
    Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Rect2f(0.4, 7.2, 4.2, 0.35); color = ink)
    Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Rect2f(1.0, 1.45, 3.0, 0.35); color = COLORS.cyan)
    label(1.1, 8.0, "Cathode"; size = 15, color = muted)
    label(2.5, 0.95, "Dexel Anode"; size = 15, color = muted)
    label(1.5, 2.6, "CdTe"; bold = true)

    # the photon, its stop and its charge drifting down
    zig = [
        Mke.Point2f(2.5 + 0.22 * sin(4π * t), 10.2 - 4.6 * t)
        for t in range(0, 1; length = 80)
    ]
    Mke.lines!(ax, zig; color = COLORS.beam, linewidth = 3)
    Mke.scatter!(
        ax,
        [Mke.Point2f(2.5, 5.6)];
        marker = :star5,
        markersize = 24,
        color = COLORS.beam,
    )
    for (dx, dy) in (
            (-0.3, -0.7),
            (0.25, -0.9),
            (-0.05, -1.25),
            (0.35, -1.45),
            (-0.35, -1.6),
        )
        Mke.scatter!(
            ax,
            [Mke.Point2f(2.5 + dx, 5.6 + dy)];
            markersize = 8,
            color = COLORS.cyan,
        )
    end
    arrow!(ax, (3.7, 4.6), (3.7, 2.1); color = COLORS.cyan, linewidth = 2, head = 12)
    label(
        2.5,
        10.25,
        "$(round(Int, energy)) keV Photon";
        align = (:center, :bottom),
        bold = true,
    )

    # the pulse against the thresholds (or, without `pulse`, straight to the counters)
    hit = findlast(t -> energy >= t, collect(thresholds))
    counters = pulse ? 21.6 : 9.4
    pulse ||
        arrow!(ax, (4.9, 4.4), (counters - 2.75, 1.6 + 1.75 * (hit - 1)); color = muted)
    pulse && draw_pulse!(ax, energy, thresholds; ink, muted, label)

    # the counters, one per bin
    for (k, threshold) in enumerate(thresholds)
        upper = k < length(thresholds) ? "–$(thresholds[k + 1])" : "+"
        node!(
            ax,
            (counters, 1.6 + 1.75 * (k - 1)),
            "Bin $(k): $(threshold)$(upper) keV";
            w = 5.2,
            h = 1.4,
            accent = BIN_COLORS[k],
            fill = k == hit ? (BIN_COLORS[k], 0.25) : card,
            textcolor = ink,
            titlesize = 16,
        )
    end
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        counters + 2.8,
        1.6 + 1.75 * (hit - 1);
        text = "+1",
        align = (:left, :center),
        fontsize = 20,
        font = :bold,
        color = BIN_COLORS[hit],
    )
    return ax
end
draw_pulse!

The pulse of counting_dexel! against its thresholds, and the arrow to the bin it counts in.

"The pulse of `counting_dexel!` against its thresholds, and the arrow to the bin it counts in."
function draw_pulse!(ax, energy, thresholds; ink, muted, label)
    hit = findlast(t -> energy >= t, collect(thresholds))
    arrow!(ax, (4.6, 1.6), (6.3, 1.6); color = muted)
    keV(e) = 1.6 + 6.6 * e / 80
    arrow!(ax, (6.6, 1.6), (14.6, 1.6); color = muted, head = 12)
    label(14.6, 1.2, "Time"; align = (:right, :top), size = 15, color = muted)
    pulse = [
        Mke.Point2f(6.8 + 7.4 * t, keV(energy * (t / 0.3) * exp(1 - t / 0.3)))
        for t in range(0, 1; length = 120)
    ]
    for (k, threshold) in enumerate(thresholds)
        crossed = energy >= threshold
        Mke.lines!(
            ax,
            [6.6, 14.6],
            [keV(threshold), keV(threshold)];
            color = BIN_COLORS[k],
            linewidth = 2,
            linestyle = :dash,
        )
        label(
            14.8,
            keV(threshold),
            "$(threshold) keV";
            align = (:left, :center),
            size = 15,
            color = crossed ? BIN_COLORS[k] : muted,
        )
    end
    Mke.lines!(ax, pulse; color = ink, linewidth = 3.5)
    label(
        10.3,
        9.7,
        "Pulse Height ∝ Energy";
        align = (:center, :bottom),
        size = 16,
        color = muted,
    )

    arrow!(ax, (17.4, keV(energy) - 0.3), (18.8, 1.6 + 1.75 * (hit - 1)); color = muted)
    return nothing
end
bowtie_fan!

A tube, its bowtie filter and the fan it shapes, on ax (a canvas about (-6.5, 6.5, -4.6, 7.6)): the central ray crosses the thin middle of the bowtie, the edge ray its thick flank, so the fan's edge gets fewer and harder photons.

"""
A tube, its bowtie filter and the fan it shapes, on `ax` (a canvas about `(-6.5, 6.5, -4.6,
7.6)`): the central ray crosses the thin middle of the bowtie, the edge ray its thick flank, so
the fan's edge gets fewer and harder photons.
"""
function bowtie_fan!(ax; dark = false)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    muted = dark ? COLORS.night_muted : COLORS.muted
    source = Mke.Point2f(0, 6.4)
    half = deg2rad(25)
    edge = [
        source + 10.0f0 * Mke.Point2f(sin(φ), -cos(φ))
        for φ in range(-half, half; length = 50)
    ]
    Mke.poly!(ax, vcat([source], edge); color = (COLORS.beam, 0.18), strokewidth = 0)
    Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = COLORS.cyan, linewidth = 9)
    # the bowtie: thin at the middle, thick at the flanks
    xs = range(-2.2, 2.2; length = 40)
    top = [Mke.Point2f(x, 5.0) for x in xs]
    bottom = [Mke.Point2f(x, 4.75 - 1.1 * (x / 2.2)^2) for x in reverse(xs)]
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        vcat(top, bottom);
        color = (COLORS.muted, 0.55),
        strokecolor = ink,
        strokewidth = 1.5,
    )
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        2.5,
        4.6;
        text = "Bowtie",
        align = (:left, :center),
        fontsize = 16,
        color = muted,
    )
    Mke.scatter!(ax, [source]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
    Mke.scatter!(ax, [source]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        0,
        7.2;
        text = "Tube",
        align = (:center, :bottom),
        fontsize = 16,
        font = :bold,
        color = ink,
    )
    for (φ, name, style) in ((0.0, "Centre", :solid), (0.92half, "Fan Edge", :dash))
        tip = source + 10.0f0 * Mke.Point2f(sin(φ), -cos(φ))
        Mke.lines!(ax, [source, tip]; color = ink, linewidth = 2.5, linestyle = style)
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            tip + Mke.Point2f(0, -0.6);
            text = name,
            align = (:center, :top),
            fontsize = 16,
            font = :bold,
            color = ink,
        )
    end
    return ax
end

1. The Phantom

The Gammex 472: a 33 cm solid-water body with seven calcium rods (50 to 600 mg/mL) on an inner ring and seven iodine rods (2 to 20 mg/mL) on an outer ring, 28 mm each. The label mask (512 × 512 at 35 cm, 16 slices over 1 cm) goes to the GPU; its material table stays on the host.

phantom_cpu = BS.create_gammex_472(
    n_voxels = 512,
    n_slices = 16,
    fov_cm = 35.0,
    z_cm = 1.0,
);
phantom = BS.Phantom(
    to_gpu(phantom_cpu.mask),
    phantom_cpu.materials,
    phantom_cpu.voxel_size,
    phantom_cpu.origin,
    phantom_cpu.extent,
);
# where the body and every rod are, for the drawings
GAMMEX = gammex_layout(phantom_cpu);

2. The Scanner

The documented NAEOTOM Alpha, NAEOTOM_ALPHA, in its standard mode: native CdTe dexels at a 0.34 × 0.364 mm pitch summed digitally 2 × 2 after counting (1376 columns of 0.373 mm and 144 rows of 0.399 mm at the isocentre), an arc detector with the quarter-detector offset, a 50 cm scan field behind the large-body bowtie, and a 1.6 mm CdTe sensor whose response (absorption, charge sharing, electronic noise, the anti-scatter grid) is BasisMonteCarlo's Geant4 table. See the scanners page for where each value comes from.

<details><summary><strong>A realistic unit: its defects and their corrections</strong></summary>

Each native dexel counts on its own, Poisson, sharing photons with its neighbours, and piles up at its own rate (27 ns dead time). Its native dexels' gains spread by 2 % and their thresholds by 0.35 keV, a fixed pattern that would ring the image uncorrected. Scatter (the Geant4 library's kernels for the Alpha) is simulated inside simulate! and corrected there from the recorded counts alone; pile-up and then the flat field are corrected after it, each with a calibration from simulated air scans.

</details>

3. Protocol and Dose

140 kVp, 0.5 s rotation, 1200 views, 5 mm collimation, 0.9 mm titanium added: the physical Gammex scan, which ran at 174 mA and reported a CTDIvol of 10.12 mGy. A tube's output per mA is its own and the simulator's source is generic, so one factor, DOSE_SCALE, scales the tube current until the simulated CTDIvol (BasisSimulator's Monte Carlo dose in the 32 cm body phantom) equals the physical scan's. The noise is then that of the dose the physical scan delivered.

"The NAEOTOM Alpha's 140 kVp axial protocol at tube current `mA`."
alpha_protocol(mA) = BS.CTProtocol(
    kVp = 140,
    mA = mA,
    views = 1200,
    rotation_time = 0.5,
    collimation_mm = 5.0,
    additional_filters = [("Ti", 0.9)],
);
1.242892857790513
# The tube-current scale that makes the simulated CTDIvol equal the physical scan's
DOSE_SCALE = let physical = (mA = 174.0, ctdi_vol_mGy = 10.12)
    p = alpha_protocol(physical.mA)
    physical.ctdi_vol_mGy / BS.compute_dose(BS.dose_source(scanner, p), p).ctdi_vol_mGy
end
protocol = alpha_protocol(174.0 * DOSE_SCALE);

4. Physics, Draws and the Image Grid

The physics switches of the basis-spectral-denoising Alpha model. Quantum noise, patient scatter (the Alpha's Geant4 kernels, superposed on the phantom's own rays) and the focal-spot blur are on. The switches that model a scintillator (fill factor, optical crosstalk, the scintillator efficiency table, lag) are off: the CdTe detector's efficiency, fill and charge sharing are already in its Monte Carlo response. The heel effect is off.

Everything before the noise (the projection through the phantom, sub-views included) is the same for every draw, so it is computed once, on the noise-free draw (keep_projection = true), and every other draw reuses it (projection) with only its own noise drawn, bit-identical to simulating each afresh.

DrawNoiseSeedUsed for
referenceoff—the noise-free expectation every result is compared with
calibrationon9234fixing the spectral pair, never measured
measuredon1234every result below

The reconstruction grid is the physical scan's clinical series: 512 × 512 over 35 cm, twelve 0.4 mm slices.

<details><summary><strong>Why <code>viewsamples = 5</code> and <code>viewarc = 1.0</code>: view integration</strong></summary>

A detector integrates while the gantry turns, so each view reads the transmitted intensity averaged over the arc it sweeps: a blur of the object, largest far from the isocentre, that the noise, counted once per view, does not share. view_samples = 5 samples that arc with five sub-views per view (the midpoint rule; at the edge of a 35 cm field they are 0.2 mm apart, a third of a pixel), and view_arc = 1.0 because a photon-counting detector reads for the whole view period. Without it the simulated signal is sharper, relative to its noise, than a physical scanner's.

</details>

"The Alpha model's physics switches for one draw."
draw_options(; seed, use_noise) = BS.SimOptions(
    seed = seed,
    use_noise = use_noise,
    projector = :dd_fast,
    use_focal_spot = true,
    use_heel_effect = false,
    # sub-views per view: the arc the gantry turns while a view is read
    view_samples = 5,
    view_arc = 1.0, # a photon-counting detector integrates for the whole view period
);
# basis-spectral-denoising's seeds: draw r of the Gammex has seed 1234 + 1000 (r − 1); its
# calibration draw is draw 9
DRAWS = (
    reference = (seed = 1234, use_noise = false),
    calibration = (seed = 1234 + 1000 * (9 - 1), use_noise = true),
    measured = (seed = 1234, use_noise = true),
);
recon_opts = BS.ReconOptions(
    matrix_size = (512, 512, 12),
    fov_cm = 35.0,
    z_cm = 12 * 0.04, # twelve 0.4 mm slices
);

5. Simulate: simulate! and spectral_basis

simulate! runs the whole photon-counting detector model on the GPU: polychromatic forward projection of every sub-view through the Monte Carlo detector response, the patient scatter, the counts of every native dexel (Poisson, neighbours covarying through the photons they share), its pile-up and the digital 2 × 2 sum. It then corrects the counts in a scanner's order, with the workspace's calibration (calibrate(scanner, protocol, recon_opts, phantom), made once from simulated scans, never from the model's own matrices). It returns

  • pcct_sino.bins: four corrected sinograms $h_k = -\log(y_k / I_{0,k})$, [col, row, view];

  • I0_bins: the air count of every ray in every bin, [col, row, bin];

  • projection, with keep_projection = true: everything before the noise, for the next draw;

  • dose: the DoseReport of the beam.

spectral_basis(ws; I0) is read from the same workspace: the response the simulation applied, passed through each ray's own bowtie transmission, so the decomposition inverts exactly what was simulated and needs no calibration scan. It checks that the response sums to I0 in every ray and bin, and refuses a basis that does not. It does not depend on the noise, so one basis serves every draw.

<details><summary><strong>The order of the corrections, and why</strong></summary>

First the pile-up: scans of air and two water cylinders at rising tube currents give each ray's pile-up-free counts from its recorded counts in every bin, its rate and its spectrum. Then the dexels' gains: low-flux scans of air and of water slabs 5–50 cm thick, each dexel's against the nominal detector's (its gain in every bin as the patient hardens the beam). Last the scatter, estimated from the corrected counts, the patient taken as water: the estimate is a nominal dexel's, and subtracted before the other two corrections it would leave each dexel's gain error on its scatter, as rings.

</details>

acquisition = let
    projection = nothing
    model = nothing
    channels = Dict{Symbol, Vector{Array{Float32, 3}}}()
    seconds = Dict{Symbol, Float64}()
    # the scanner's calibration, as a scanner is calibrated: the pile-up from air and water scans at
    # rising currents; the flat field from low-flux scans of air and water slabs (each dexel's gain
    # per bin, and how it changes as the patient hardens the beam)
    calibration = BS.calibrate(
        scanner,
        protocol,
        recon_opts,
        phantom;
        sim_opts = draw_options(; DRAWS[:reference]...),
    )
    # the noise-free draw first: it projects
    for name in (:reference, :calibration, :measured)
        opts = draw_options(; DRAWS[name]...)
        t0 = time()
        ws = BS.create_workspace(scanner, protocol, opts, recon_opts, phantom; calibration)
        try
            # the dose and the projection do not depend on the noise: both come from the first draw;
            # simulate! corrects in a scanner's order: pile-up, flat field, then the scatter
            sim = BS.simulate!(
                ws,
                phantom,
                protocol,
                opts;
                capture_raw_counts = false,
                report_dose = projection === nothing,
                keep_projection = projection === nothing,
                projection = projection,
            )
            projection === nothing && (projection = sim.projection)
            # the four corrected bins
            channels[name] = [Array(b) for b in sim.pcct_sino.bins]
            if model === nothing
                # [n_cols, n_rows, n_bins]
                I0 = Float32.(Array(sim.I0_bins))
                model = (
                    I0 = I0,
                    # ray-resolved spectral model
                    basis = BS.spectral_basis(ws; I0 = I0),
                    geom = ws.geom,
                    dose = sim.dose,
                )
            end
        finally
            BS.release_backend!(ws)
        end
        seconds[name] = time() - t0
    end
    (; channels, seconds, model...)
end;

6. The Four Energy Windows

A photon stops in a dexel's CdTe and frees a charge that drifts to the dexel's anode; the pulse it makes is as tall as the photon's energy, and the highest threshold it crosses decides the bin that counts it (top left). Bottom left: what each bin detects on the central ray, the absolute response the decomposition uses, against the energy the photon arrived with. The windows overlap because charge sharing, electronic noise and K-fluorescence escape let a photon register below its true energy; the spikes are tungsten's characteristic lines.

The bowtie (top right) is thin at the middle of the fan and thick at its edges: it cuts the flux toward the edge and hardens what is left, so the high bins fall off less than the low ones (bottom right). One scalar I0 per bin could not describe this, which is why the basis is resolved per ray.

7. The Chain's Settings

The denoiser is generalized HYPR-LR in both domains, BS.SpectralHYPR(), the chain of basis-spectral-denoising:

  • projection domain (ProjectionHYPR): within each detector row, each ray's split of its total count across the four bins is pooled over a 3 × 3 (column × view) window whose view neighbours are two views apart (view_stride = 2), so the odd and even views stay independent. Neighbours are weighted by how likely their total count is under the ray's own, and each ray keeps its own total. The count dispersion of every bin is measured from the air rays.

  • image domain (ImageHYPR): the reconstructed basis pair is rewritten as the minimum-noise VMI (the composite) and a complement whose noise is uncorrelated with it. The composite is kept as reconstructed, so its resolution and noise texture are FDK's; the complement, which carries only spectral information, is pooled within its slice with likelihood weights on the composite, over the window width (3 to 41 pixels) with the least estimated risk. Every noise level comes from the difference of the odd- and even-view reconstructions.

Nothing in the chain averages detector rows or slices.

projectionkernelHYPRKernel(3 × 3, local linear)dispersion:measuredview_stride2imagecandidates132537411515621731841noise_window15
HYPR_CHAIN = BS.SpectralHYPR()
VMI_ENERGIES = (40, 70, 100, 140);
# The decomposition and reconstruction settings of the chain; ACNR is added on the measured draw
VMI_CHAIN = (
    method = :nchannel,
    controls = BS.NChannelControls(),
    use_tlbf = false,
    antialias = true,
);

The reconstruction windows. BS.PairFilter filters the composite, whose window sets the resolution and noise texture at the minimum-noise energy, and the complement, whose window sets how that changes away from it. Each window is an apodized ramp, $W(f) = \exp(-(f/f_c)^p)$ on the grid-Nyquist axis, sampled at 11 knots as a CustomFilter. basis-spectral-denoising fitted the Alpha's pair once, to the physical Gammex scan's MTF at every energy and its NPS shape (VMI, Br36f, QIR 0, 0.4 mm, 350 mm): composite $f_c = 0.5$, $p = 2$; complement $f_c = 0.45$, $p = 6$.

Why the composite and the complement, not water and iodine?

The water and iodine images' noise is strongly anti-correlated, and a VMI near the minimum-noise energy is quiet only where both were filtered alike. The composite and its complement have uncorrelated noise, so each can have its own window.

A window is defined on the frequency axis of the grid it is applied on, so on a grid other than the fitted one (512² over 35 cm) its argument is rescaled by the ratio r of the grids' bandlimits (BS.grid_bandlimit). This notebook uses the fitted grid, so r = 1.

ALPHA_WINDOWS = (composite = (fc = 0.5, p = 2.0), complement = (fc = 0.45, p = 6.0));
PAIR_FILTER = let knots = Tuple(range(0.0, 1.0, length = 11))
    # the grid the windows were fitted on: the Alpha's clinical series, 512² over 35 cm
    fitted = BS.CTGeometry(
        scanner;
        n_angles = protocol.views,
        fov_cm = 35.0,
        z_cm = 0.48,
        collimation_mm = protocol.collimation_mm,
    )
    r = BS.grid_bandlimit(acquisition.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size) /
        BS.grid_bandlimit(fitted, (512, 512, 12))
    window(q) = BS.CustomFilter(
        knots,
        Tuple(round(exp(-(x * r / q.fc)^q.p), digits = 5) for x in knots)
    )
    (
        filter = BS.PairFilter(
            window(ALPHA_WINDOWS.composite),
            window(ALPHA_WINDOWS.complement),
        ),
        r = r,
    )
end;

8. The Spectral Pair, Fixed from the Calibration Draw

spectral_pair measures, from the odd- and even-view halves of a reconstruction, the minimum-noise energy $E^*$ and the complement's coefficient $\beta$. Near its minimum the VMI noise hardly changes with energy, so the argmin of one acquisition is itself noise and would move from draw to draw; it is a property of the scanner and protocol, so it is measured once, on the calibration draw, and fixed for every other draw, the noise-free one included:

  • pair_basis = (Estar, β): from the calibration draw decomposed without denoising and reconstructed with a standard soft-tissue window (SoftFilter); the pair the windows act on;

  • composite_energy: the minimum-noise energy of the same draw after the projection-domain HYPR, which moves it; the composite ACNR and the image HYPR act on.

Estar81.0β0.003349composite80.0
PAIR_BASIS = let ch = acquisition.channels[:calibration], I0 = acquisition.I0
    decompose(channels) = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
        channels,
        basis = acquisition.basis,
        geom = acquisition.geom,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
        vmi_energies = VMI_ENERGIES,
        keep_sinograms = true,
        use_acnr = false,
        VMI_CHAIN...,
    ).sinograms
    p = HYPR_CHAIN.projection
    d_none = decompose(ch)
    d_proj = decompose(BS.hypr_lr(
        ch,
        I0;
        kernel = p.kernel,
        dispersion = BS.estimate_dispersion(ch, I0),
        view_stride = p.view_stride,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
    ))
    sp(d; kw...) = BS.spectral_pair(
        d.water,
        d.iodine,
        acquisition.geom,
        recon_opts.matrix_size;
        filter = BS.SoftFilter(),
        antialias = VMI_CHAIN.antialias,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        kw...,
    )
    x = sp(d_none)
    c = sp(d_proj; basis = (Estar = x.Estar, β = x.β))
    (Estar = x.Estar, β = x.β, composite = c.Estar)
end

9. One Call: vmi_pipeline

One call runs the whole chain on the measured draw. Every detector row is kept and reconstructed onto the twelve-slice grid; the decomposition is the K-channel maximum-likelihood estimator (method = :nchannel) with its published controls; ACNR (on by default) acts on the complement only, before the image HYPR. The noise-free draw goes through the same call without the denoiser and ACNR: the reference, reconstructed exactly as its noisy counterpart.

vmi = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
    channels = acquisition.channels[:measured],
    basis = acquisition.basis,
    geom = acquisition.geom,
    to_backend = to_gpu,
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
    vmi_energies = VMI_ENERGIES,
    denoiser = HYPR_CHAIN,
    fbp_filter = PAIR_FILTER.filter,
    pair_basis = (Estar = PAIR_BASIS.Estar, β = PAIR_BASIS.β),
    composite_energy = PAIR_BASIS.composite,
    VMI_CHAIN...,
);
reference = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
    channels = acquisition.channels[:reference],
    basis = acquisition.basis,
    geom = acquisition.geom,
    to_backend = to_gpu,
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
    vmi_energies = VMI_ENERGIES,
    fbp_filter = PAIR_FILTER.filter,
    pair_basis = (Estar = PAIR_BASIS.Estar, β = PAIR_BASIS.β),
    composite_energy = PAIR_BASIS.composite,
    use_acnr = false,
    VMI_CHAIN...,
);

10. Basis Images and VMIs

The chain's basis pair: iodine as a mass density (mg/mL) and water as a density (g/mL), the central slice. Every VMI is synthesized from this one pair with the monoenergetic attenuation of water and iodine; no energy-dependent filtering is applied.

11. Accuracy and Noise

The phantom's labels are resampled onto the reconstruction grid (resample_to_recon).

QuantityHow it is measured
rod HUthe mean over a disk of 60 % of the rod's radius, all twelve slices
water regionthe solid water eroded with erode_mask_2d(…; erode_px = 12) in every slice: its mask blurred by a 12-pixel Gaussian and kept where the blur stays above 0.999, about 3σ (2.5 cm) clear of the body's edge and of every rod
theoretical HU$1000\,(\mu_E - \mu_{E,\mathrm{water}})/\mu_{E,\mathrm{water}}$ of every material, from its composition
noise-free HUthe same quantity on the noise-free reference: its error against theory is the bias of the basis model itself
noise σthe standard deviation of the measured VMI minus the reference within one slice, RMS over the slices: the phantom's structure and any deterministic artefact cancel
pcct_results = let
    energies = Float64.(vmi.energies)
    nz = size(vmi.vmis, 3)
    labels = BS.resample_to_recon(phantom_cpu, acquisition.geom, recon_opts.matrix_size)
    water_mask = cat(
        (
            collect(BS.erode_mask_2d(
                labels[:, :, z] .== UInt8(BS.REGION_SOLID_WATER);
                erode_px = 12.0,
            ))
            for z in 1:nz
        )...;
        dims = 3,
    )
    theory_hu(material, E) = let μw = BS.compute_μ_at_energy(BS.XA.Materials.water, E)
        1000 * (BS.compute_μ_at_energy(material, E) - μw) / μw
    end
    material(label) = phantom_cpu.materials[Int(label) + 1]

    # a disk of 60 % of the rod's radius about its centroid, in every slice
    function rod_roi(label)
        pixels = findall(==(UInt8(label)), labels[:, :, (nz + 1) ÷ 2])
        cx, cy = mean(p -> p[1], pixels), mean(p -> p[2], pixels)
        radius = 0.6 * sqrt(length(pixels) / π)
        [
            (i - cx)^2 + (j - cy)^2 <= radius^2
            for i in axes(labels, 1), j in axes(labels, 2), _ in 1:nz
        ]
    end
    # measured against theoretical at one energy: least-squares slope, intercept and R²
    function fit(x, y)
        slope = sum((x .- mean(x)) .* (y .- mean(y))) / sum(abs2, x .- mean(x))
        intercept = mean(y) - slope * mean(x)
        r2 = 1 - sum(abs2, y .- (intercept .+ slope .* x)) / sum(abs2, y .- mean(y))
        return (; slope, intercept, r2)
    end
    groups = ( # the region labels of the rods, BS.REGION_CA_50 … and BS.REGION_I_2_0 …
        Ca = (
            labels = UInt8.(10:16),
            names = ["50", "100", "200", "300", "400", "500", "600"] .* " mg/mL",
        ),
        I = (
            labels = UInt8.(20:26),
            names = ["2.0", "2.5", "5.0", "7.5", "10.0", "15.0", "20.0"] .* " mg/mL",
        ),
    )
    rods = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
    for (group, g) in pairs(groups)
        rod_labels = g.labels
        measured = zeros(length(rod_labels), length(energies))
        noise_free = similar(measured)
        theoretical = similar(measured)
        for (row, label) in pairs(rod_labels)
            roi = rod_roi(label)
            for (column, E) in pairs(energies)
                measured[row, column] = mean(vmi.vmis[:, :, :, column][roi])
                noise_free[row, column] = mean(reference.vmis[:, :, :, column][roi])
                theoretical[row, column] = theory_hu(material(label), E)
            end
        end
        fits = [
            fit(theoretical[:, column], measured[:, column])
            for column in axes(measured, 2)
        ]
        rods[group] = (names = g.names, measured, noise_free, theoretical, fits)
    end
    # per-slice standard deviation in the water ROI, RMS over the slices
    slice_noise(volume, column) = sqrt(mean(
        abs2,
        [std(volume[:, :, z, column][water_mask[:, :, z]]) for z in 1:nz],
    ))
    difference = vmi.vmis .- reference.vmis
    (
        energies,
        labels,
        water_mask,
        rods,
        water_mean = [mean(vmi.vmis[:, :, :, c][water_mask]) for c in eachindex(energies)],
        water_reference = [
            mean(reference.vmis[:, :, :, c][water_mask])
            for c in eachindex(energies)
        ],
        water_theory = [theory_hu(material(BS.REGION_SOLID_WATER), E) for E in energies],
        water_noise = [slice_noise(vmi.vmis, c) for c in eachindex(energies)],
        water_noise_vs_reference = [
            slice_noise(difference, c)
            for c in eachindex(energies)
        ],
        water_pixels_per_slice = count(water_mask) ÷ nz,
        finite = all(isfinite, vmi.vmis) && all(isfinite, reference.vmis),
    )
end;

The Solid Water

The eroded solid-water region (left) and its mean HU at each energy, measured (bars) and on the noise-free reference (diamonds). The phantom's solid water is modelled with the composition of water, so its theoretical HU is 0 at every energy (dashed line).

The Noise

The noise is what is left when the noise-free reference is subtracted from the measured VMI (left, at 40 keV, in the water region of one 0.4 mm slice); its per-slice standard deviation is the noise σ at each energy (right). The standard deviation of the measured VMI itself differs from it by at most 0.04 HU at any energy, so the ROI holds noise only. The noise is highest at 40 keV, where the synthesis weights the iodine image most heavily and so amplifies its noise, and changes little from 70 keV up, where the VMI is mostly the composite and the water image.

The Rods against Theory

Each rod is measured in the dashed disk drawn on it (top). Solid lines are the measured HU of each rod, dashed lines its theoretical HU.

The decomposition represents every voxel as iodine plus water. The solid water and the iodine rods are close to that basis; calcium is not exactly a combination of iodine and water at every energy, so its VMIs carry a small, energy-dependent model error on top of the noise. The per-rod table below separates the two with the noise-free reference.

Linear Regression

The same rods (drawn above), measured HU against theoretical HU at each energy, with the least-squares line. The dashed line is identity.

Per-Rod Error

Measured minus theoretical HU for every rod at every energy, and in brackets the same for the noise-free reference: the bias of the iodine–water basis model itself, which no amount of dose would remove. The difference between the two is what the noise and the denoiser add. The largest relative error of the measured draw is 28.7 % over the iodine rods and 5.1 % over the calcium rods; of the noise-free reference, 9.5 % and 7.0 %.

checks = let
    r = pcct_results
    list = NamedTuple[]
    addcheck(name, value, pass) = push!(list, (; name, value, pass))
    addcheck(
        "spectral basis reproduces I0 in every ray and bin (max rel. error)",
        round(acquisition.basis.I0_relerr; sigdigits = 2),
        acquisition.basis.I0_relerr < 5.0e-5,
    )
    addcheck(
        "simulated CTDIvol equals the physical scan's 10.12 mGy",
        round(acquisition.dose.ctdi_vol_mGy; digits = 2),
        abs(acquisition.dose.ctdi_vol_mGy - 10.12) < 0.05,
    )
    addcheck(
        "all four bins decomposed",
        vmi.settings.n_channels,
        vmi.settings.n_channels == 4,
    )
    addcheck("every VMI value finite (measured and reference)", r.finite, r.finite)
    addcheck(
        "decomposition: fraction of rays not converged",
        vmi.quality.frac_not_converged,
        vmi.quality.frac_not_converged < 1.0e-3,
    )
    water_error = maximum(abs, r.water_mean .- r.water_theory)
    addcheck(
        "solid water within 10 HU of theory at every energy (largest error, HU)",
        round(water_error; digits = 1),
        water_error <= 10,
    )
    reference_error = maximum(abs, r.water_reference .- r.water_theory)
    addcheck(
        "noise-free solid water within 10 HU of theory at every energy (largest error, HU)",
        round(reference_error; digits = 1),
        reference_error <= 10,
    )
    fits = [f for g in (:Ca, :I) for f in r.rods[g].fits]
    slopes = [f.slope for f in fits]
    addcheck(
        "rod regression slope within 1 ± 0.1 at every energy (min, max)",
        (round(minimum(slopes); digits = 3), round(maximum(slopes); digits = 3)),
        all(s -> abs(s - 1) <= 0.1, slopes),
    )
    r2 = minimum(f.r2 for f in fits)
    addcheck(
        "rod regression R² at least 0.99 at every energy (smallest)",
        round(r2; digits = 4),
        r2 >= 0.99,
    )
    list
end;

Summary

calibration = BS.calibrate(scanner, protocol, recon_opts, phantom)  # once per scanner and protocol
ws    = BS.create_workspace(scanner, protocol, opts, recon_opts, phantom; calibration)
sim   = BS.simulate!(ws, phantom, protocol, opts; keep_projection = true)  # then (…; projection)
basis = BS.spectral_basis(ws; I0 = sim.I0_bins)          # ray-resolved, no calibration scan
vmi   = BS.vmi_pipeline(; channels = sim.pcct_sino.bins, basis, geom = ws.geom,
                          to_backend, matrix_size, vmi_energies = (40, 70, 100, 140),
                          denoiser = BS.SpectralHYPR(), fbp_filter = PAIR_FILTER.filter,
                          pair_basis, composite_energy)

Four photon-counting energy windows go into the decomposition as four measurements, and the spectral model is the one the simulation applied, ray by ray through the bowtie, so no calibration scan is involved.
